c.tagline: Poland's city of a hundred bridges, hidden bronze dwarfs, and a grand medieval square.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; booking through an app (Bolt, Free Now or iTaxi) is usually cheaper and easier than a street hail.

emergency.note: 112 is the pan-European emergency number reaching police, fire and ambulance; operators generally speak English.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the packed Rynek nightlife crowds and on busy trams, and keep an eye on drinks in clubs.

hood_desc: Wrocław's showpiece heart, built around one of Europe's largest medieval market squares (Rynek) with its Gothic Old Town Hall, colourful merchant houses, St. Elizabeth's Church and dozens of the city's beloved bronze dwarfs; the walkable base for first-timers.

The oldest, most atmospheric part of the city on islands in the Odra, home to the twin-towered Cathedral of St. John the Baptist, cobbled lanes lit by gas lamps at dusk and the Botanical Garden; quiet, sacred and photogenic.

A formerly run-down 19th-century district north of the river now reborn as Wrocław's creative quarter, full of murals, artist studios, craft cafes and vintage shops; best for travellers chasing an offbeat, bohemian side of the city.

An up-and-coming riverside district just east of the centre with regenerated tenements, breweries, restaurants and a growing bar scene; good for those who want to be near the action but off the tourist track.

A large, leafy residential district south of the centre with early-20th-century villas, parks and everyday local life; suits travellers and families wanting a calmer base with easy tram links to the centre.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though some locals prefer bottled for taste.

transit.pay: Buy single or time tickets from onboard machines (cards accepted), street ticket machines, or apps like jakdojade, mPay or moBILET; contactless bank-card tap-to-pay works on many trams and buses. A single-ride ticket costs about 4.60 PLN (~$1.25) and a 24-hour ticket about 15 PLN (~$4).
transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 5am–11pm, with a network of night lines covering the city through the small hours.

bus: Wrocław Bus Station (beneath the Wroclavia mall, by Wrocław Główny)

transit.m: MPK city bus 106 to Wrocław Główny railway station, ~40 min
MPK bus 206 to the centre, ~40 min

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving about 10% for good service in restaurants is appreciated. State the total you want to pay when handing over money, as simply saying 'thank you' can be taken to mean 'keep the change'.

food.name: Pierogi
food.desc: Hand-pinched dumplings boiled or pan-fried, filled with ruskie potato and curd, meat, cabbage and mushroom, or seasonal fruit, and topped with fried onion.

places.name: Pierogarnia Stary Mlyn
places.note: Rustic mill-themed pierogi house with the widest range of fillings in the centre.

places.name: Pierozak Pierogarnia Wroclawska
places.note: Family-run, budget-friendly, with an open kitchen where you watch them folded.

places.name: Gluten Appetit
places.note: Dumplings made with Lower Silesian mill flour; good gluten-free options too.

food.name: Zapiekanka
food.desc: Poland's open-faced baguette pizza: half a loaf loaded with mushrooms and cheese, grilled until bubbling, then drenched in ketchup and garlic sauce.

places.name: Tostoria
places.note: Hole-in-the-wall counter locals rate for a cheap, properly crisp zapiekanka.

places.name: Hala Swiebodzki
places.note: Old railway station turned street-food hall with several late-opening grill counters.

places.name: Hala Targowa
places.note: 1908 market hall; snack stalls under the concrete arches do quick baked baguettes.

food.name: Sledz
food.desc: Salted herring served cold in oil with onion, or in soured cream with apple; the classic Polish accompaniment to a chilled shot of vodka.

places.name: Konspira
places.note: Solidarity-themed restaurant where herring and vodka come as a matched set.

places.name: Mleczarnia
places.note: Candlelit old-Jewish-quarter bar with vintage clutter and good vodka snacks.

places.name: Karczma Lwowska
places.note: Lviv-style tavern on the main square doing full-blown traditional Polish starters.

food.name: Zurek
food.desc: Sour rye soup with white sausage, potato and a halved boiled egg, often ladled into a hollowed bread bowl. Tangy, smoky and very filling.

places.name: Restauracja Kurna Chata
places.note: Country-cottage bistro serving Polish classics from breakfast to late dinner.

places.name: Bar Mleczny Mis
places.note: Wroclaw's most famous milk bar, feeding students near the university for decades.

places.name: Bar Mleczny Mewa
places.note: Milk bar inside the market hall; the one locals name first, and dirt cheap.

food.name: Kluski slaskie with rolada
food.desc: The Silesian Sunday plate: dimpled potato dumplings and rolled beef roulade stuffed with bacon and pickle, with braised red cabbage and dark gravy.

places.name: Restauracja Jadka
places.note: Refined Polish cooking in Gothic vaults just behind the town hall.

places.name: Restauracja Kurna Chata
places.note: Generous, homely regional plates at prices well below the square's tourist spots.

places.name: Bar Mleczny Pod Temida
places.note: Handwritten daily menu, minimal tourists, the most authentic milk-bar experience.

food.name: Paczki
food.desc: Deep-fried yeast doughnuts filled with rose-petal jam or plum, glazed and scattered with candied orange peel. Eaten by the million on Fat Thursday.

places.name: Charlotte Chleb i Wino
places.note: Bakery-cafe on the main square; pastries in the morning, wine in the evening.

places.name: Cukiernia Sowa
places.note: Long-established Polish patisserie with reliably fresh rose-jam paczki.

places.name: Hala Targowa
places.note: Market-hall bakery stalls sell them by the bag, still warm, for small change.

food.name: Polish craft beer
food.desc: Lower Silesia has one of Poland's liveliest brewing scenes, from unfiltered pilsners to sour ales, and Wroclaw pours it a taster-flight at a time.

places.name: Targowa Craft Beer & Food
places.note: Local and guest taps under the market hall, with five-beer tasting boards.

places.name: Pinta
places.note: Two dozen rotating taps from one of Poland's pioneering craft breweries.

places.name: Pod Latarniami
places.note: Small bar with a remarkable bottled-beer list alongside its taps.

food.name: Nalewka and flavoured vodka
food.desc: Home-style fruit and herb liqueurs, from sour-cherry wisniowka to honey and hazelnut, poured ice-cold in shot glasses beside a plate of herring.

places.name: Konspira
places.note: Long list of Polish vodkas and nalewki served in a 1980s underground setting.

places.name: Mleczarnia
places.note: Atmospheric, cheap and open late; the local choice for a slow nalewka.

places.name: Karczma Lwowska
places.note: Tavern pouring house-infused liqueurs alongside its Galician menu.

landmarks: Market Square (Rynek)
One of Europe's largest medieval squares, ringed by candy-colored burgher houses and buzzing café terraces at the vibrant heart of Wrocław's Old Town.
Old Town Hall (Stary Ratusz)
A Gothic masterpiece crowned with an astronomical clock and lacy pinnacles, this 13th-century hall is Wrocław's most photographed civic building.
Ostrów Tumski (Cathedral Island)
Wrocław's oldest quarter, where gas lamps are still lit by hand each evening amid cobbled lanes, bridges and soaring church spires.
Cathedral of St. John the Baptist
A twin-towered Gothic cathedral rebuilt after wartime ruin; ride the lift up its tower for sweeping views over the Odra River islands.
Centennial Hall (Hala Stulecia)
Max Berg's pioneering 1913 reinforced-concrete dome, a UNESCO World Heritage landmark fronted by a dancing multimedia fountain and vast pergola.
Wrocław's Dwarfs (Krasnale)
Hundreds of whimsical bronze gnomes hide on street corners citywide, a playful tribute to the anti-communist Orange Alternative movement that visitors love hunting.
Racławice Panorama
A colossal 114-meter circular painting from 1894 that immerses viewers in the 1794 Battle of Racławice with astonishing 360-degree realism.
University of Wrocław & Aula Leopoldina
The Baroque university headquarters conceals the Aula Leopoldina, a jaw-dropping frescoed ceremonial hall, plus a Mathematical Tower with rooftop city views.
St. Elizabeth's Church
Climb the 91-meter tower of this Gothic basilica beside the Rynek for the finest panorama of Wrocław's spire-studded skyline.
Hydropolis
A slick interactive science center devoted entirely to water, housed in a 19th-century underground reservoir—perfect for rainy days and curious kids.

intl.to: Berlin (Germany) - via Poznań or the Cottbus regional link

train.note: Wrocław Główny is a striking neo-Gothic station in the middle of the city. PKP Intercity runs to Warsaw in about 3h40, Kraków in 3 and Poznań in 2, with international services to Prague and Berlin - the Berlin route has improved with the Cottbus regional connection. Book on the Intercity site for the cheaper advance fares.

bus.note: Coaches use the terminal at the Wroclavia shopping centre beside Wrocław Główny. FlixBus and RegioJet run to Prague in about 5 hours and to Berlin, Vienna and Kraków. Carry your passport or EU ID card. The coach is often cheaper than the train on the Prague run.

ferry.note: Wrocław sits on the Odra with a dozen islands and many bridges, but the river carries only summer sightseeing boats rather than scheduled services, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Świdnica
half.blurb: A handsome town whose UNESCO-listed timber-framed Church of Peace is one of the largest wooden Baroque churches in Europe, about an hour from Wrocław.

half.name: Książ Castle
half.blurb: Poland's third-largest castle, dramatically set above a wooded gorge near Wałbrzych, with terraced gardens and wartime tunnels.

full.name: Karpacz & the Karkonosze Mountains
full.blurb: A mountain resort at the foot of Śnieżka, gateway to hiking in Karkonosze National Park and the quirky wooden Wang Church.

full.name: Kłodzko Valley
full.blurb: A scenic borderland of spa towns, the vast Kłodzko Fortress and the Table Mountains' labyrinth of rock formations.
